text:
alex: quick sync — trying to reconcile the internal runtime surface across hosted / dedicated / private. RFC sketch currently lists a minimal HTTP surface but ops wants eviction/drain hooks. want to agree on a compact, safe contract.

jin: can you paste the minimal shape you're proposing?

alex: sure, here's what I had in mind (very rough):
```json
{
  "paths": {
    "infer": "/v1/infer",
    "stream": "/v1/stream",
    "health": "/v1/health"
  },
  "meta": { "tenant_id": "string", "mode": "hosted|dedicated|private" }
}
```

sara: evict/drain on hosted is scary. hosted customers shouldn't be able to call host-level evictions. those signals should come from our control plane (leader -> runtime) not via public runtime endpoints. :thinking:

maya: 100% agree. For private deployments it's fine to expose ops endpoints, but only when the customer opts into exposing them to the control plane. must be behind feature flags, and every call needs audit metadata.

tom: also need to clarify fallback semantics — when dedicated pool is overloaded, hosted routing should fall back to compatible variant. That logic belongs in the router, not the runtime surface.

alex: thinking of a two-tier contract to make this explicit:
- core surface (MANDATORY): infer, stream, health, meta. identical across all hosting modes. lightweight, safe.
- ops surface (OPTIONAL): evict, drain, rebind, admin-health. only enabled when the manifest declares the capability and is signed by the control plane / customer key.

alex: example manifest registration (proto-ish):
```json
{
  "manifest_version": 1,
  "service": "runtime-adapter",
  "capabilities": ["core"],
  "optional_capabilities": ["ops:evict","ops:drain"],
  "signed_by": "controlplane@example.com",
  "signature_ttl": "24h"
}
```

sara: nice. implementation notes: when optional_capabilities includes ops endpoints, Console must show them and we must enable additional RBAC + retention (audit traces). Also we should disallow ops endpoints on hosted unless explicitly allowed in the tenant contract.

maya: +1. For private we should default to ops surfaced but clearly document responsibility: customer owns KMS keys + audit retention. add a telemetry flag so we can detect accidental exposures.

jin: how do we handle versioning? small change to core surface should be non-breaking. optional ops can be versioned independently and must be registered as part of the manifest handshake.

alex: proposal for handshake flow: 1) runtime boots, fetches manifest from control plane OR reads local manifest (private). 2) runtime exposes only the capabilities declared. 3) control plane verifies signature and pushes routing policies that depend on declared capabilities. 4) console shows capability matrix per deployment.

ops-bot: deploy-check: runtime-manifest v1 signed ok for cluster/runtime-42 — no ops endpoints enabled.

tom: one more edge: what about on-prem sidecars that need to rebind secrets? we should include a small "rebind" ops endpoint but require HSM/KMS prove-of-possession in the manifest.

alex: yeah — require a key thumbprint claim in manifest for any rebind-like capability. otherwise deny.

maya: +thumbsup. can we add this as an RFC follow-up item and a checklist for Console, router, and runtime?

alex: will draft RFC follow-up with the two-tier contract, handshake flow, and manifest schema. will ping infra + security for the signature/KMS bits.

sara: sweet, thanks.

jin: thanks — leaves me less worried about hosted surface creep. :thumbsup:
